beats.text: You're talking to someone. You both want to leave. But nobody says it.
Or you'd love to keep going. And so would they.
Researchers asked over a thousand people when they wanted their conversations to end.
Only about two percent ended when both people wanted.
In about half, both wanted to talk less. In about one in ten, both wanted more.
And here's the catch. People had no idea what the other person wanted.
Their guesses were off by more than half the conversation.
So you're not awkward. Nobody can see the exit.
Next time, just say it. Kindly. They might be relieved.

sources: Mastroianni, Gilbert, Cooney & Wilson (2021). Do conversations end when people want them to? PNAS. Study 1: 806 people; Study 2: 252 strangers in the lab. ~2% ended when both wanted; ~30% when one wanted; ~half both wanted less; ~10% both wanted more; guesses about the partner off by ~64% of conversation length (Scientific American).
